## Notes

- Aircraft Characteristics Charts, printed as 4.44A (Commonwealth, jp2 111-112), 4.44b (Italian, jp2 143) and 4.44c (German, jp2 143-144, its continuation misheaded 4.44b); the rules call them 34.6. Read twice, from the archive.org scan and from the community chart PDFs (Commonwealth Charts.pdf pp. 1-2, Axis Charts.pdf pp. 1-2): 1224 cells compared, 1 differs, and only in convention (the Italian C 200 Saetta's range, printed ';40' with a stray mark, recorded as 40).
- Each nation has two sub-tables: fighters and fighter-bombers (table: fighter; mission columns F, S, R, D) and bombers, flying boats, transports and reconnaissance (table: bomber; D, R, B, Transport). Fighters need a pilot; the others do not.
- Columns: range in hexes (a '*' marks drop tanks; '**' a range for transfer missions only); tac_air, the air-to-air rating (in parentheses: the aircraft may never fly a mission on which it would start air-to-air combat); maneuver; bomb, bomb points ('n/Tm': n bomb points or m torpedo points; null: no bombs); fuel, fuel points per flight.
- Mission letters, as printed: F combat air patrol and strafing, S scramble, R reconnaissance, D strafing and any bombing, B Axis naval convoy and land support bombing, Transport what it carries (a number: TOE or replacement points; P: may drop paratroops; tons or fractions: supply). Marks: '!' capable by day; 'N' capable by day and night; '.' or null not capable; Commonwealth '0' night only in a restricted role (Blenheim IVF night scramble; Albacore night land-support or convoy bombing); 'S' strafing only (Lysander); 'A' may also strafe armour (Hurricane IID); '*' night scramble only (Bf.110, Ju.88C).
- alternative_of marks an 'or' row: the same aircraft in another configuration, chosen per mission.
- As printed and left so: Cant Z.501 tac_air '(2' (no closing parenthesis); Cant Z.506B range blank; Gladiator Mk. II fuel a dash; Beaufighter IF and VIF manufacturer blank; the B-17/D, B-26 and Bombay rows print an extra dot in the mission columns.
- Footnotes in our words: the Ar.196, Cant Z.501 and Z.506B and the Sunderland are flying boats; the Skua is a dive bomber; the Gladiator, Sea Gladiator, Swordfish and Valentia are biplanes; the C.714, D.520 and MS406 are French; the MS406, Sea Gladiator, Swordfish and Valentia never arrive as reinforcements.
